newsitem.title: USA: SEC study shows fall in class actions US fed court.
newsitem.headline: SEC study shows fall in class actions US fed court.

text.p: The number of companies sued in securities class actions in federal court dropped for the year following passage of a litigation reform measure, while the number of such suits in state courts has risen, the Securities and Exchange Commission said in a study released Wednesday.

The report submitted to the White House, was prepared by the SEC at President Clinton's request after passage of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995, a law designed to curb certain lawsuits.
Despite the agency's findings, Levitt emphasized it is too soon to tell what impact the litigation reform has had.

"The commission endorses the ultimate conclusion of the report: it is too early to assess with confidence many important effects of the Reform Act and therefore, on this basis, it is premature to propose legislative changes," Levitt wrote to President Clinton in an April 15 letter.
Levitt said he would continue monitor the issue.
